test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Shirin __came off with a brilliant idea__ to solve the problem.

options.text: came up with a brilliant idea
came off on a brilliant idea
came off to a brilliant idea
came up in a brilliant idea

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrasal verb **"came up with"** means **to think of or suggest an idea, plan, or solution**. (कोई विचार सुझाना)
 
• In the sentence, Shirin generated a solution — hence, “came up with” is the correct expression.
 
• The original phrase **"came off with"** is incorrect here. "Come off" usually means to succeed or happen, not to generate an idea.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Shirin **came up with**__ a brilliant idea to solve the problem."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "came off on"** – Incorrect and ungrammatical; no such phrasal verb exists in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "came off to"** – Incorrect usage; “come off to” is not used to indicate idea generation.
 
• **Option 4: "came up in"** – Incorrect preposition; “came up in” doesn’t fit idiomatically with ideas.
